《伪美多迪乌斯启示录》
就体现了这种立场，认定罗马帝国是抵御敌基督的唯一屏障，罗马皇帝是基督徒的领袖：“离了她（即罗马帝国），这世上的一切统治和权威都失了效力。即使有人向她开战，也不能战胜她，所有冲撞她的民族都会被她消灭……哪里有、将来又哪里会有比她更强的王国或其他权势呢？”
成文稍晚的
《伪但以理启示录》
也持类似观点。
这些作者都认为，帝国的正统与帝国的胜利相伴而行。691/692年君士坦丁堡召开会议（“五六会议”）时，与会教士致查士丁尼二世的开幕文辞说道，基督的神恩已经遍覆大地，无知和谬误已经让位于知识，并说：“基督我们的上帝，掌着这艘最大的船，即整个世界的舵，如今立您在我们之上。您是明智的统领、虔敬的皇帝，实为我们的保护者。您出言明辨，永远守护真理，在大地上施行审判与正义，行在无可指摘的道路上。”

In spite of these considerations, there is little to suggest that the blanket of Christian beliefs and devotional practices that covered the Roman Empire in the period up to the early Arab conquests was not relatively complete, even if there survived within its fabric a wide range of beliefs and practices, tolerated, or not, by the local church depending upon circumstances, and whether or not explicitly proscribed in the canons of the church. By the same token, the consonance of Christianity and the Roman Empire was also taken for granted. If opposition to imperial monotheletism had generated for a while a dissenting view, yet such a view was not adopted by the church within the empire, indeed it was limited largely to the few high-profile individuals who enunciated it most publicly, and to the papacy. Such ideas and arguments certainly inflicted some damage on the political fabric of the state in the west in the 640s and 650s, but the crushing of dissent by the imperial government and the confirmation of the imperial position at the council of 662 put an end to this particular problem.

And after 680–681 the unequivocal identification of the Christian Roman state and its emperor with Christianity and with God’s kingdom on earth was once again unchallenged in the writings of churchmen and theologians in the West and within the empire. In the canons of the Quinisext, the Christian empire is contrasted with the heathen who assail it from without.

Andrew of Crete, writing in the early eighth century in an oration in praise of the birth of the Virgin, was absolutely clear that Christianity would triumph since for him the civilized world was already Christian, paying reverence to Christ and taking pride in their Christian name.
Even in the former eastern provinces, where miaphysite hostility to the imperial church remained, Christian thinkers could assume an eventual Roman victory. The
Apocalypse of Ps.- Methodius

, composed in the early 690s in Singara, certainly reflected this position and in doing so identified the Roman Empire as the only defense against the Antichrist and the Roman emperor as the leader of the Christian people: “For all rule and authority of this world are rendered null and void apart from her (i.e., the Roman empire). For war is also made upon her and she is not overcome, and all the nations which dash themselves against her will be destroyed by her. . . . For where is, or where will there be, a kingdom or another power that excels her?”
A slightly later apocalyptic text, that of
Ps.- Daniel
, presents a similar view.

All these writers assumed the parallel between imperial orthodoxy and imperial success. The opening address of the assembled clergy to the emperor Justinian II at the council of 691/692 in Constantinople (the “Quinisext”) notes that the divine grace of Christ has covered the earth, that ignorance and error have been exchanged for knowledge and that “Christ our God, who steers this greatest of ships, the entire world, has now set you over us, the wise governor, the pious emperor, our protector indeed: you who dispense your words in discernment, safeguard truth always, render judgment and justice upon earth and walk in the blameless path.”
共享的叙事，共同的忠诚？
Shared Narratives, Common Loyalties?

这些观念反映出一个较长期的过程，在这一过程中，东罗马的基督教，也就是帝国的基督教，逐渐同《圣经》中的往事交织在一起。越来越多的日常宗教实践被比照于《圣经》中的先例，助长了这个过程。帝国识字的精英和教士以外的人在多大程度上接受了这些观念，尚难确定。不过，正如我们将看到，这套理解世界的方式在很大程度上通过教士，以及人们经常接触的地方教会和讲道，传给了更广泛的听众。适合的经文，尤其是《新约》经文，被引入礼仪，也让参与者亲身融入仪式的实践和演绎，进一步传播了这些观念所体现的态度与信仰。正如一位评论者指出的，全年各种礼仪活动的演绎和仪式，让教士与会众进入圣史叙事中的人物角色，逐渐认同叙事所描绘的事件和时代，使所有参与者共享一套叙事，并在不同社会阶层和地域之上强化一套共同的预设。
我们已经提到，人们越发看重圣餐礼，把它当作基督徒宗教实践的主要标志，这当然是同一过程的一部分。值得注意的是，东罗马教会的礼仪历似乎正是在七世纪后半叶和八世纪初统一起来的，说明这些变化正在加速。
通过礼仪的演绎以及教士的在场与布道，帝国的居民和那些已经脱离帝国统治的各地居民，都知道自己同属一个道德宇宙。

Such ideas expressed a longer-term process through which eastern Roman— imperial— Christianity became interwoven with the biblical past. This was encouraged through ever-increasing parallels between the religious practice of the everyday and biblical antecedent. The extent to which such ideas reached beyond the literate elite of the empire or the clergy remains open to question, although as we will see much of this way of understanding the world reached a much wider audience through the medium of the clergy and regular contact with the local church and its preaching. But the attitudes and beliefs these ideas embodied were also promoted through the integration of the celebrants themselves into liturgical practice and into the liturgical drama through the introduction of appropriate texts, especially from the New Testament. As one commentator has pointed out, the performance and ritual activities associated with liturgical celebration across the year draw those involved, clergy and congregation, into the roles of those represented in the sacred narratives, forging an identity with the events and the times they depict, promoting a common shared narrative among all participants, and reinforcing a common set of assumptions across social and geographical space.

The growing emphasis that we have noted already on the eucharist as the key marker of Christian observance was one aspect of this process, of course. Importantly, it seems to have been during the second half of the seventh and early eighth centuries that the east Roman liturgical calendar was standardized, reflecting the increasing pace of these processes.

Through both liturgical performance and the presence and preaching of the clergy, the inhabitants of the empire, as well as of all those regions no longer under imperial rule, knew that they were members of a common moral universe.

在各行省、较大的城市中心以外，教会布道起了多大作用？这个问题很难回答。布道辞（homilies，即“交谈”）本是给会众听的。虽然常常很长，讲的却是与“普通”基督徒有关的神学和道德价值。除了措辞特别艰深的作品外，听众很可能通常都能听懂。程式化表达、反复申说、耳熟能详的主题和故事，以及浅白直截的语言，都有助于理解。但这些布道能在多大程度上影响人们的想法和态度，则取决于布道的情境与频次。晚期罗马世界那些人口稠密的城市为此类布道提供了理想的场所，证据也表明布道常能奏效。
然而自640和650年代起，教士所面对的世界已大不相同，城市在不断萎缩。在君士坦丁堡，或许还有塞萨洛尼基，城市环境意味着既有的布道方式得以延续。

How effective was the preaching of the church in the provinces and away from the larger urban centers? This is a difficult question— sermons (homilies, i.e., “conversations”) were intended for a congregation, and although often very long, dealt with theological and moral values relevant to the “ordinary” Christian. That the texts themselves were usually understood, except for some particularly high-language compositions, is more than likely— formulaic constructions, repetition, well-known motifs, and stories as well as straightforward language all contributed. Their purchase on people’s minds and attitudes, however, depended on context and frequency, and while the populous cities of the late Roman world provided an ideal forum for such forms of preaching— and the evidence suggests that they were often effective

— churchmen had to confront a very different, deurbanizing world from the 640s and 650s. In Constantinople, or perhaps Thessaloniki, the urban environment meant that the established patterns of preaching could continue.

许多别的城市无疑也是如此，但克里特的安德烈或格尔马努斯等人的七世纪后期和八世纪讲道辞，无论在结构还是主题上，都有迹象表明发生了一些重要变化。首先，布道越来越常在常规礼仪之外举行，例如在日课和守夜礼中。其次，比起此前几个世纪，主题更偏重经文评析或释义，或围绕特定的节日，为平信徒解释《旧约》和《新约》中特定经段的意义。五六会议要求每天都要讲道，尤以星期日为重，并特别嘱咐教士务必遵从教父的诠释，切勿任意作出自己的解释：“如果谈及某一段经文，切不可作出与教会先贤及圣师在著作中所定不同的解释。应当如此求取卓越，而非自行撰述，因为他们有时力所不及，结果反而有失体统。”

The same was no doubt true of many other urban contexts, but there are interesting indications in both the structure and the themes of later seventh- and eighth-century homiletic compositions by preachers such as Andrew of Crete or Germanus that some important changes had taken place. First, sermons were increasingly delivered outside the standard liturgies, during the offices and vigils. Second, their subjects tended to concentrate more than in the preceding centuries on scriptural comment and exegesis or on specific feasts, explaining to the laity the significance of specific passages from the Old and New Testament. The Quinisext insists that homilies should be preached on a daily basis, most particularly on Sundays, and is most particular that clergy should not indulge in their own interpretations but follow those of the Fathers of the church: “If a Scriptural passage should come up for discussion, they shall in no wise interpret it differently than the luminaries and doctors of the church have set down in their writings. In this way shall they distinguish themselves, rather than by composing their own works, being at times incapable of this and thereby falling short of what is proper.”

这是否反映出当时有人认为民众对教会所传的基本道理置之不理，尚不清楚。不过这段话接着说：“因为通过上述教父的教导，民众得以认识要事与美德，分辨何者无益，何者当弃。他们由此改过自新……不至为无知的情欲所俘。他们留心这些教导……因惧怕临头的惩罚而努力得救。”至于教堂里的布道和会众的举止，西奈的阿纳斯塔修斯在一篇讲道辞中也曾指出，实际的虔敬举止有时和我们所想的不同。布道者一啰唆，人们就打哈欠、打瞌睡。有的没听完就走了，有的临到领圣餐才到，一领完就急匆匆地走。有人七嘴八舌谈起日常事务、钱财或类似的世俗话题，干扰布道，这样的事很常见。甚至还有男人站在一旁，色眯眯地盯着在场的女子。

Whether this reflected a perception that people were failing to pay attention to the basic message of the church is unclear, but the passage continues: “For through the teaching of the aforementioned Fathers the people are given knowledge of important things and virtues, and of unprofitable things and those to be rejected: thus they reform their lives. . . and escape being taken captive by the emotions of ignorance; giving heed to this teaching they. . . work out their salvation in fear of the punishments hanging over them.” And on the topic of preaching in church and the behavior of the congregations, Anastasius of Sinai notes in one of his own sermons that pious behavior was not always what we may imagine it to have been: people yawn and doze off if the preacher is too long-winded; some leave before he has finished, others show up only just before communion before rushing off as soon as they are finished; disruptive chattering and gossip about matters of day- to-day business, money, or similar secular topics is common; men even stand around ogling the women who might be present.

阿纳斯塔修斯的评论所指是城市社会还是乡村社会，并不清楚。也许两者兼有。当然，他谈的是巴勒斯坦和叙利亚的人，而非帝国行省的居民。不过如我们所见，帝国的罗马权威所受到的新政治边界限制，此时还几乎没有触及普世的基督教世界。乡村的布道可能与城镇很不相同，主要是因为乡村聚落较为隔绝，基本的读写能力远为低下，而具备适当资质的教士也为数有限。那些在640年代之前城市化程度很高的行省，到了七世纪后半叶，城市化程度越来越低。此外，遭受敌人袭扰的地区非常不安全，似乎常使高级教士也逃离，以致民众无法与教会当局经常接触。第18条教规命教士回到自己的会众中，第37条则处理因同一原因远离教座的主教的情形。五六会议第19条教规坚称教士只能依据教父的书面文字，这透露了教会此次所遇问题的性质。另外几条教规多为四、五世纪教会会议规定的重申，提及教会内部诸种失序现象，如行省主教间的权力冲突，以及教士无故离开教座或堂区（例如第17、20、25、80条）。这些教规显示了维持行省教士的纪律和教会日常活动的困难。这种局面也使行骗、误解、异端及疏于遵守礼仪更容易发生。例如，第60条谴责假装被邪魔附身的人，规定他们必须遭受为确实受此侵扰的人所施的痛苦驱魔礼。第63条规定销毁伪造的殉道记，第68条禁止毁弃《旧约》或《新约》的书册，或将它们拆开供制香者使用。

It is not clear whether Anastasius’s comments refer to urban or rural society— perhaps both. And of course he is talking about people in Palestine and Syria rather than in the provinces of the empire, although, as we have seen, the newly imposed political limits on imperial Roman authority still barely impacted on the ecumenical Christian world. Preaching in the countryside was likely a very different affair from in towns, chiefly because of the relative isolation of rural settlements, the much lower levels of basic literacy, and the limited number of appropriately qualified clergy. Those provinces that had been heavily urbanized before the 640s were in the second half of the seventh century increasingly less so. Furthermore, the high level of insecurity in those regions exposed to hostile raids seems often to have meant a flight of even senior clergy, thus depriving the populace of regular contact with ecclesiastical authority. Canon 18 orders the return of clergy to their flocks, while canon 37 deals with bishops who live away from their sees for the same reason. The insistence in canon 19 of the Quinisext that clergy rely only on the written word of the Fathers hints at the nature of the problem the church faced here. Several other canons, mostly repeated from councils of the fourth and fifth centuries, refer to a range of disorders within the church, such as conflicts of authority between provincial bishops or unwarranted absences from their sees or parishes (canons 17, 20, 25, and 80, for example). These indicate the difficulties of maintaining both clerical discipline and the regular activities of the church in the provinces. Such a situation also meant increased possibilities for fraudsters, for misunderstanding, for heterodoxy, for laxness of observance. Canon 60, for example, condemns those who feign possession by demons and ordains that they should be subject to the painful rites of exorcism applied to those who were genuinely so afflicted; canon 63 ordains the destruction of false martyrologies while canon 68 prohibits the destruction of volumes of either Old or New Testaments or their dismemberment for the use of perfumers.

这个共同的道德宇宙，覆盖并不均匀，它触及其中各成员的方式也各不相同。不过，敬奉圣徒和殉道者的实践与信念仍然巩固了它。供奉他们的教堂与崇拜中心遍布帝国各行省，对他们的敬奉把整个社会维系在一起，从行省各社会阶层的普通民众，到社会精英、教会和皇室成员，都由此建立了联系。重要的是，这些崇拜同时具备地方性，且行于整个帝国。所有圣徒、殉道者和使徒都属于天上的众圣，他们在上帝面前为人类代求。人们相信，他们也保护尘世王国免遭敌人侵害。代表这些众圣的，又是一位全帝国的主保，即上帝之母（Theotokos）。从六世纪后半叶起，帝国宫廷尤其提倡尊她为君士坦丁堡的主保圣者，也因而以她为整个帝国命运的护佑者。
君士坦丁堡本身也供奉行省的圣徒。例如查士丁尼一世曾在君士坦丁堡捐建约三十座教堂，其中不少献给在帝国远方备受敬奉的圣徒。圣狄奥多尔的崇拜以本都的欧凯塔为中心，却早已流行于各地。许多行省教堂献给圣塞尔吉乌斯，他的崇拜原盛于叙利亚边疆。此外，还有来自伊苏里亚的圣特克拉，以及圣斯特凡诺斯、圣尼古拉斯、圣乔治等许多圣徒，有的远没有这么有名。
通过广为流传、为各地所共享的圣徒崇拜，行省居民获得了对本地和区域的认同，也就是一种行省的“乡土之爱”。与此同时，他们彼此相系，也与帝国的中心君士坦丁堡相联。那里供奉着许多同样的圣徒和殉道者，并直接受到童贞玛利亚的护佑。

This shared moral universe was thus somewhat patchy in its coverage, variable in the way it reached its members. But it was reinforced nevertheless by practices and beliefs associated with the devotion accorded to saints and martyrs, whose churches and cult centers were spread throughout all the provinces of the empire, and devotion to whom established a bond across the whole of society, among ordinary provincials of all social strata as well as members of the social elite, the church, and the imperial household. Importantly, these were both local and empire-wide at the same time. All the saints, martyrs, and apostles were part of the heavenly host that interceded with God on behalf of humankind but who also protected, so it was believed, the earthly kingdom from its enemies. And they were represented in turn by an empire-wide patron, the Mother of God, the Theotokos, who from the second half of the sixth century had been promoted by the imperial court in particular as a patron saint of Constantinople and hence of imperial fortunes more broadly.

Constantinople itself also housed the saints of the provinces. Justinian I had endowed some thirty churches in Constantinople, for example, many for saints popular in distant parts of the empire: St. Theodore, whose cult was already widespread although centered at Euchaïta in the Pontus; St Sergius, for whom many churches in the provinces were built but who was at home on the Syrian frontier; St. Thecla from Isauria; St. Stephen; St. Nicholas; St. George; and many more, some of them far less well-known.

The point is that through the widespread and shared cults of saints, people in the provinces received both a sense of local and a regional identity, a provincial “patriotism,” but were at the same time linked one to another and to the seat of empire, Constantinople, the home of many of the same saints and martyrs and a city that stood under the direct protection of the Virgin Mary.
圣徒崇拜产生了一系列共同的敬奉活动和相关实践，有的关乎医治，有的关乎驱除邪魔，有的为了防备人力不能控制的各种险患，尽管各地做法有别。例如，佩戴护身符以驱除邪魔，是相当普遍的做法。圣髑崇拜所具有的实践性质，把人们对圣徒代祷之力的信赖，同一种确信结合在一起，即圣徒通过圣髑而有形地临在，是使代祷生效所必需的媒介。
至迟到了七世纪，身体遗存、曾接触身体的物件，
或因各类遗存所体现的圣徒在场而成圣的油，都已经成为代祷过程中的重要要素。
殉道者崇拜几乎每天都有纪念活动，在所耗时间和敬奉的心力上，已能与庆祝基督生平与受难的大礼仪等量齐观。
献给特拉蓬的
颂辞
与阿尔忒弥奥斯的奇迹集表明，人们相信身体上的接触对代祷和祷求的医治极为重要。这些圣徒施行医治时，触摸与身体接触是不可缺的一环。对圣徒遗物或其圣所不敬、加以亵渎，也可能招来不幸。行省的一则圣狄奥多尔奇迹故事这样写道：

Saints’ cults generated a range of devotional and related practices in common, even if regionally divergent, connected with healing, with the driving out of evil spirits, with protection against the vast range of hazards outside human control. The wearing of amulets aimed at warding off evil spirits was common and widespread, for example. The practical nature of the cult of relics integrated a belief in the intercessory powers of a saint with a conviction that a physical presence, through the saint’s relics, was an essential facilitating medium.
Physical remains, such as bodies, objects that had had touched bodies,
or oil sanctified by the saint’s presence in the form of physical remains of one sort or another, had certainly by the seventh century become vital aspects of the intercessory process.
The cult of martyrs, with almost daily commemorations, came to equal the great liturgical occasions celebrating aspects of the life and passion of Christ in time and devotional energy.
The
laudatio

for Therapon and the collection of miracles of Artemius show how important physical contact was believed to be for the process of intercession and the associated healing for which prayers were offered. When these saints healed, touch and physical contact were an essential element. Mistreating or abusing saintly relics or the saint’s sanctuary could also have unpleasant consequences, as one of the provincial miracle accounts of St Theodore relates:

那时，那可憎的敌族挤满我们的城，正在这里过冬。他们的首领不知受了什么邪魔的恶意驱使，下令拿镐和撬杠对付圣徒那极其美丽、悦人心目的圣所，意图把它彻底捣毁，直至地基。他于是把手下全召进这座备受尊崇的圣所，把他的恶毒计划告诉他们。但话还没说完，上帝的震怒就临到他身上。他一头栽倒在地，满地打滚，口吐白沫，咬着舌头。蛮族匆忙抬起他，把他安置在他自己的住处。如此一来，他那魔鬼般的图谋中道而止，和他作对的邪灵却没有放过他。

At that time, when that hateful race of enemies filled our city and were spending the winter there, their leader happened to be moved by some demonic malice, and he ordered a number of picks and levers to be used against the most beautiful and pleasing shrine of the saint, with the intention of destroying it utterly as far as its foundations. So he summoned all his men into the said honoured shrine and explained to them his evil plan concerning it. But while the words were still in his mouth, God’s anger rose up against him and he fell headlong to the ground, rolling about, foaming at the mouth and chewing his tongue. The barbarians, snatching him up, laid him to rest in his own lodging; and while in this way he was cut short in his satanic undertaking, yet he was not released from the hostile spirit that opposed him.

然而，礼敬圣髑与圣徒的圣所得到了官方认可，与圣徒崇拜有关的许多做法则没有。关于邪魔、病痛及各种肉身和灵性苦难的缘由与医治手段，人们抱有根深蒂固的信念与忧虑，因此“迷信”的做法很多，尽管有着基督教的外观。与崇拜中心有关的奇迹故事，反映了这种混合之下常见的传说与异事。许多做法已很接近甚至等同于魔法，但圣者和修道士常常也从事一模一样的活动。例如，六世纪吕基亚的锡永圣尼古拉斯的奇迹故事写到，他曾从一棵树里赶出邪魔，并向不同的圣徒献祭动物。据说，七世纪初加拉太的西凯翁圣狄奥多尔，也曾把一群意外逃出的邪魔赶回它们逃出的山洞。九世纪初，圣修士约安尼基乌斯则让熊听从自己的吩咐，以此向比提尼亚一些村民展示上帝赐给他的力量。

这样的故事还能举出许多，早已形成了相当固定的题材。其他许多故事同样带有奇幻色彩，讲到斩龙、喂养其他野兽、召出清泉，等等。除此之外，还有更常见的卧祷治病，即在圣徒的小堂或墓室过夜，梦见圣徒前来为病人治病。不同圣徒的信众对于各自主保谁更灵验，意见并不一致。以自己喜爱或奉为主保的圣徒之名诅咒或惊呼，也是日常言谈的一部分。五六会议的一些教规谈到了某些问题和实践，透露了教会处理民间那些常带迷信色彩的信仰时所面临的难处。

Many of the practices associated with the cult of saints were not officially sanctioned, however, unlike the focus on relics and the shrines of the saints. Entrenched beliefs and anxieties about evil spirits, the causes and cures for disease and various forms of physical or spiritual affliction, meant that “superstitious” practices abounded, albeit in a Christian guise. The miracle stories associated with cult centers reflect tales and wonders typical of this mix, and while much of this was not far from or tantamount to magic, holy men and monks were often involved in exactly the same sorts of activities— the miracles of the sixth-century saint Nicholas of Sion, in Lycia, have him involved in driving out evil spirits from a tree as well as sacrificing animals to various saints, for example; St. Theodore of Sykeon in early seventh century Galatia is likewise credited with driving evil spirits back into a hole in the hill from which they had accidentally been released, while the holy monk Ioannicius in the early ninth century demonstrates his divinely granted powers to a group of villagers in Bithynia through making a bear do his will.

Again, the stories can be multiplied and represent a well-established stock. Many other stories are equally fantastic, entailing the slaying of dragons, the feeding of other wild beasts, the calling forth of springs of fresh water, and so forth, quite apart from the more usual cures affected through incubation (sleeping in the saint’s chapel or crypt overnight and dreaming that the saint comes to cure the patient). Devotees of individual saints disagreed about the relative efficacy of their patron; for example, cursing or exclaiming by the name of one’s favorite or patron saint was part of everyday speech. And several canons of the Quinisext council address questions and practices suggestive of some of the issues the church faced in dealing with popular and often superstitious beliefs.

不过，这一切都应放在七世纪中叶已经牢固确立的基督教世界里理解。这个世界中的某些群体起着重要的联结作用。例如，帝国各地无论城镇还是乡村，修道士都同各行省的城乡居民直接接触。毋庸置疑，他们有助于传播共同的信念和理解世界的方式，以及借着日常的敬奉与实践对世界施加影响的方式。当然，修道士有时也会造成扰乱、甚至成为危险因素，威胁既有秩序，五六会议为此制定了规条。七世纪上半叶归于约翰·莫斯库斯、阶梯约翰名下的著作收集了修道士和圣者事迹，西奈的阿纳斯塔修斯的《问答录》也谈及这些人的作用。这些记载表明，他们在这方面颇为重要。
要紧的是，他们在整个罗马世界传播了一种共享的基督徒认同。这种认同既以基督徒的身份来表达，也以罗马人的身份来表达。两者在象征和政治文化上的价值及含义，实际上是等同的。

不过也有证据显示，至少在帝国疆域内，自七世纪中叶至八世纪后期，修道士的地位可能有所下降，作用也比往日小了。当然有例外。面临波斯、继而阿拉伯人的入侵，巴勒斯坦的修道士向西迁移，索弗罗尼乌斯和马克西姆就在其中。西奈的阿纳斯塔修斯也是同样显赫的人物。但例如就安纳托利亚而言，除了五六会议所关注的修道纪律和公共场合举止之外，关于大型修道中心和修道活动的消息寥寥无几。原因之一可能是，阿拉伯人的入侵和袭扰直接破坏了乡村面貌与许多城镇的环境。在许多行省，这种环境的变化必然影响修道士的人数，也影响他们能否过上相对安稳的修道生活。

Still, all this is to be understood within what was, by the middle of the seventh century, a solidly Christian world. It was a world in which certain groups played an important connective role. Monks, for example, were throughout the lands of the empire, in both town and country, in direct contact with the people of the provinces, in towns and villages, and undoubtedly acted as a mode of transmitting commonly held beliefs and ways of thinking about the world as well as acting upon it in respect of day- to-day piety and practice. They might also, of course, act as a disruptive or even dangerous element at times, threatening the established order— hence the regulatory canons of the Quinisext. Collections of tales about the deeds of monks and holy men, such as are found in the writings ascribed to John Moschus or John Climacus in the first half of the seventh century, as well as the references to the role of such men in the Questions and Answers of Anastasius of Sinai suggest their importance in this respect.

The material point is that they acted to transmit notions of shared Christian identity across the Roman world, an identity that was clearly expressed as much in terms of Christian as in that of Roman— the two were effectively equivalent in their symbolic and political-cultural value and implications.

Yet there is also evidence suggesting that, within the empire at least, monks may have lost some of their status and played a lesser role than hitherto in the period from the middle of the seventh century into the later eighth century. Of course there were exceptions— the Palestinian monks who moved westward in the face of the Persian and then the Arab invasions, Sophronius and Maximus among them, while Anastasius of Sinai is a similarly outstanding figure. But of major monastic centers and monastic activities in Anatolia, for example, other than the issues of monastic discipline and public comportment that came to the attention of the Quinisext, very little is heard. One reason for this may have been the physical disruption to the rural landscape as well as to many urban contexts following from the Arab invasions and raids, a change in context that must have impacted on both numbers as well as on the possibilities for a reasonably secure monastic existence in many provinces.
第二个可以清楚辨认的群体是基层教士。他们负责确保人们遵守正统礼仪，按规程定期举行圣餐礼，并把经文的讯息如实传达、讲解给绝大多数民众。教会试图使各行省的宗教实践保持一致，故五六会议的许多教规都以这些教士为对象。
在城镇以外的乡村腹地，他们是高级教士和普通民众之间的主要联络人，有时还是唯一的联络人。他们也是民众在信仰上经常受到教导的唯一来源。然而，我们对他们的活动、教育程度与读写水平，乃至人数，所知甚少。并非每个共同体都有教堂或司祭。教会的组织大体以城市及其主教为中心，由主教任命所谓的
chōrepiskopoi
（乡村主教）照管城镇周围的乡村共同体。但这些教士的权威和职权都非常有限。到了787年尼西亚会议时，他们实际上已降至与普通司祭相同的地位。

A second clearly identifiable body was constituted by the regular clergy, for it was they who were responsible for ensuring that orthodox observance was respected, that the eucharist was celebrated properly and at the assigned intervals, and that the message of scripture was faithfully transmitted and explicated to the vast majority of the population. It was they who were the focus for many of the canons of the Quinisext as the church attempted to maintain the uniformity of practice across the provinces.

In the rural hinterland, they were the main, if not the only, contact between the senior clergy and the ordinary populace and the only regular source of teaching about the faith. But we know very little of their activities, their level of education and literacy, or, indeed, their numbers. Not every community had a church or a priest; the organization of the church was largely focused on the city and its bishop, who appointed so-called
chōrepiskopoi

(country bishops) to care for the rural communities around the towns, although these clergy had very limited authority and powers; by the time of the council of Nicaea in 787, they had been reduced effectively to the status of regular priests.
七世纪初，一些村庄没有教堂或小堂，也没有常驻教士给村民灵性的照管与教导，这似乎并不罕见。
《西凯翁的狄奥多尔传》

提到了村里的司祭，但他们显然并非乡村社会处处皆有。按照查士丁尼时代的法律，地方上的小堂和教堂大多由本地土地所有者或村社负责，似乎没有充分纳入教会的管理体系。这在五六会议的教规中有所反映，其中有些条文涉及在这些地方主持宗教事务的教士。他们即使能得到报酬，也是由当初捐建小堂或教堂的地主或村社支付。一些教士由主教的经费供养，但以此方式获得报酬的占比不明。许多教士的生计要么靠堂区居民为教士提供的服务而捐赠，要么靠以教堂捐建者的佃户身份经营其所租种的田地。
在七世纪中叶起许多行省所面临的形势下，这种情况不大可能有所改善。因此不免要问，教会在这类地区到底有多大的影响力。证据显示，直到八世纪后期和九世纪，许多乡村才形成了能有效运作的教会组织。
证据还表明，当时虽已萎缩的城市中心，依然是主教及其会众之间至关重要的联系纽带。令人意外的是，研究这一时期的学者很少注意到这种作用。
In the early seventh century it seems that it was not unusual for some villages to have no church or chapel and no regular clergy attached to them for their spiritual care and education. The
Life

of Theodore of Sykeon mentions village presbyters, but they are clearly not a universal feature of rural society. According to the Justinianic legislation, local chapels and churches were largely the responsibility of local landowners or village communities and seem to have been poorly integrated into the church administration, a fact reflected to some degree in the canons of the Quinisext, some of which are concerned with the clergy who attended them— who were paid, when at all, by the landowner or the community who had endowed the chapel or church in the first place. Some clergy were supported from episcopal funds, although the proportion of those remunerated in this way is unknown, and many were supported either from donations made by the parishioners themselves in return for the services or from their own landholdings, as tenants of the person who had endowed the church.

The situation is unlikely to have improved much in the conditions that prevailed across many provinces from the middle of the seventh century, and this raises the question of just how much influence the church really had in such areas— indeed, the evidence suggests that it was only by the later eighth and ninth centuries that an effective ecclesiastical establishment had been evolved in much of the countryside.

It also suggests that the shrunken urban centers of the period continued to be a vital link between the bishops and their flocks, a role that has received surprisingly little attention in research on the period.
东罗马社会和更广大的东地中海世界，社会分层十分严重。财富与贫困，能否诉诸司法、获得权力并在强者面前维护自身利益，都构成了社会壁垒。虽然存在跨越这些壁垒的纵向联系与效忠关系，但社会不平等造成的横向分隔是整个制度的一部分。
在这样的情形下，人们对经济和社会处境的不满，有时会通过信仰及与之有关的社会实践表现出来。这并不令人惊讶，在大多数此类社会形态中都属意料之中。文献有时显示了这一点。例如，有些人对于圣徒能否有效代求、能否施行上帝所感发的医治或其他奇事，有所怀疑。同样的怀疑态度也影响了他们对社会秩序的看法，有时还影响他们的反应。不过，我们所掌握的七世纪直接证据确实很少。我还会回到这一主题。

Eastern Roman society, and society in the eastern Mediterranean world more broadly, was heavily stratified. While vertical associations and loyalties existed that cut across the barriers generated by wealth and poverty, by access or lack of access to justice, power, and the ability to defend one’s interests against the more powerful, the horizontal divisions produced by social inequality were systemic.

It is hardly surprising in such a context—as we would take for granted in most such social formations— that dissatisfaction with economic and social conditions might at times have manifested itself in terms of beliefs and related social practice. This is occasionally apparent, for example, when the texts suggest that a degree of skepticism affected what people thought about the efficacy of the saints to intercede or to affect divinely inspired cures or other wonders as well as their attitudes and at times reactions to the social order, although it is true that we have very little direct evidence for this during the seventh century. I will return to this theme later.

因此，罗马基督教文化及其中的诸多信念，和其他信仰体系一样，内部多有分歧，也容得下质疑。激烈乃至尖刻的论辩恰恰是这一时期的特点，尤其涉及刚才提到的问题。在六、七世纪，关于代祷等问题，“理性主义”与“民众取向”的观点之间的紧张尤为显著，尽管这是基督教神学思考从一开始就有的特点。比如，七世纪后半叶，西奈的阿纳斯塔修斯主张，圣徒和普通人在死后都无肉身在世，因此普通人的灵魂失去记忆、自我辨识和认识他人的一切能力，必须在这种悬而未决的状态下等待末日审判。
圣徒的灵魂虽仍保有一定的意识，但在地上代表圣徒的，是天上的天使。他们采取圣徒平素的衣着与相貌，向尘世众人展示圣灵的力量。阿纳斯塔修斯提出的一项根据是，人们往往在同一时刻于不同地方看见同一个圣徒。
六世纪后期，这种观点已经引起争议。牧首欧提基乌斯
《传记》
的作者欧斯特拉提乌斯，写过一篇论灵魂的性质以及死后灵魂和肉身关系的论著，专门反驳这类“理性主义”的说法。他明确力求给这类奇迹提供有神学根据的解释，其中，上帝干预世事、直接经由圣徒从中斡旋，都不可或缺。

Christian Roman culture and the range of beliefs it encapsulated was, therefore, by no means an undifferentiated, unquestioning monolith, no more than is any belief system. To the contrary, lively, vituperative debate was a feature of the period, particularly in regard to the issues just mentioned. In the sixth and seventh centuries in particular, the tension between a “rationalist” and “populist” perspective was very clear, in respect of intercession as well as of other issues, even if this had been a feature of Christian theological reflection from the beginning. For example, in the later seventh century Anastasius of Sinai argued that, since neither saints nor ordinary mortals have a physical presence after death, the soul of the ordinary human loses all its powers of memory, self-identity, and recognition and must await the Last Judgement in this state of limbo.

But while those of the saints do retain a degree of consciousness, it is the heavenly angels who represent them on earth, taking on their customary apparel and appearance in order to demonstrate the power of the Holy Spirit to those who inhabit the world of mortals. In partial proof of his argument, Anastasius notes that the same saint has often been observed in different places at the same time.
Such a view was debated already in the later sixth century, when Eustratius, author of the
Life

of the patriarch Eutychius, penned a treatise on the nature of the soul and the relationship it bears to the body after death, in which he set out to refute such “rationalist” arguments in an explicit attempt to provide a theologically grounded explanation for such miracles in which divine intervention and the direct mediation of God through the saints were fundamental elements.
在回应求助者祈祷而显现并代祷的圣徒是否有真实的肉身在场这个问题上，肯定圣徒亲身现形的文献，多于对灵魂与肉身关系态度谨慎、持“理性主义”解释的文献。前一种立场是诸多奇迹集的常例，包括居鲁士与约翰在亚历山大里亚所行的
奇迹
科斯马斯与达米安在君士坦丁堡所行的奇迹，
德米特里乌斯在塞萨洛尼基所行的奇迹，
新兵狄奥多尔在欧凯塔所行的奇迹，
以及阿尔忒弥奥斯
和特拉蓬在君士坦丁堡所行的奇迹
等。事实上，至阿纳斯塔修斯写作时，他的看法似乎已属少数，尽管争论在后来的几个世纪里也没有完全平息。

The texts that assume a real physical presence for the saints who appear and intercede on behalf of those who have prayed for their assistance outnumber those in which a more careful somatological or “rationalist” approach is evident. The former is the norm in collections such as the
Miracles
of Cyrus and John (in Alexandria),
of Cosmas and Damian (set in Constantinople),
of Demetrius (at Thessaloniki);
of Theodore Tiro (Euchaïta),
of Artemius (Constantinople),
of Therapon in Constantinople,
and a number of others. Anastasius seems, in fact, and by the time of his writing, to reflect a minority opinion (although the debate simmered on into later centuries).
须记住，有关代祷的争论并不局限于罗马世界。同时期，亚美尼亚和伊朗的基督徒共同体也在进行类似的争论。

这只是更广泛的争论的一个方面。争论的问题是，人的选择有多大的自由，上帝又在多大程度上干预人间的事务。圣徒传在重申神力在人间事务中的核心地位方面起着关键作用。例如，塞萨洛尼基的圣德米特里乌斯第一部奇迹集，只承认上帝的震怒和神的干预是真正的原因，并排除了生理或自然的解释。某些奇迹集汇集了各种论证，通过重述相关圣徒的奇迹和事迹确实如故事中所述那样发生，来“证明”理性主义立场错误。成书于八世纪后期或九世纪的
《尼科米底亚的以撒传》
就是一个好例子。
五六会议的教规显示，这个问题一直存在：“真理的仇敌伪造了殉道记，意欲玷辱基督的殉道者，并使听者丧失信心。我们命令不得在教堂里公开宣读这些殉道记，须将之付之一炬。至于收取这些著作或信以为真的人，我们对他们施以绝罚。”

It is important to bear in mind that this debate about intercession was not confined narrowly to the Roman world— similar debates were taking place in Armenian and Iranian Christian communities at the same time.

And this was just one aspect of a broader discussion concerning the degree of human freedom of choice and of divine intervention in human affairs, in which hagiography played a central role in reaffirming the centrality of the divine in human affairs—as in the first collection of the miracles of St. Demetrius at Thessaloniki, for example, where only the wrath of God and divine intervention are admitted as real causal factors; physiological or natural explanations are dismissed. Some collections included a variety of arguments “proving” the rationalist position wrong by repeating the fact that the miracles and acts of the saints in question had occurred in the form described in the miracle stories— a good example is found in the
Life
of Isaac of Nicomedia, for example, dating to the later eighth or ninth century.

That the issue was a constant is reflected in the canons of the Quinisext: “We command that martyrologies which have been faked by enemies of truth, in order that they may dishonor Christ’s martyrs and cause their listeners to lose faith, should not be read publicly in churches, but should be consigned to the flames. As for those who receive them or accept them as true, we anathematize them.”
不论这场持续争论有过怎样的曲折，怀疑和疑问的存在几乎毋庸置疑。例如，六世纪后期大教堂的执事多梅提阿努斯，就不肯相信西凯翁的狄奥多尔所行的奇迹。
这类怀疑或恼怒有时表现为直接行动。
早在利奥三世推行官方圣像立场之前，圣像有时就已引起争执。例如588年，帝国当局试图削减东部边疆士兵的军饷，激起了他们的怨愤。普里斯库斯将军出示了来自埃德萨、印有基督像的圣
mandylion
（巾帕），即罗马人所谓的
acheiropoiēton
（“非人手所造之像”），试图安抚骚乱的士兵。然而，据与事发年代相近的史家狄奥菲拉克特·西莫卡塔记载，士兵们看穿了这种试图慑服他们的做法，向圣像投掷石块，随后还袭击了皇帝莫里斯本人的肖像。
激怒的士兵对奉命前来安抚他们的君士坦提纳和埃德萨的主教也毫无敬意。
一个多世纪以后，727年阿拉伯人围攻尼西亚时，一个士兵向圣母像扔了一块石头，将其击损。编年史家狄奥凡尼斯在不到一百年之后撰写的
《编年史》
中记下了这件事，将这个士兵的攻击归于他的不虔敬和反圣像情绪。然而即使确有此事，它远更可能只是挫败感的一种表现。这究竟是因为相信圣像会帮助他们的民众或士兵过于天真，还是因为动手的士兵自己恼怒，我们无从知晓。

Whatever the vagaries of this ongoing discussion, there can be little doubt that there was room for skepticism and doubt, as in the case of the cathedral deacon Dometianus in the late sixth century, who refused to believe in the miracles of Theodore of Sykeon, for example.
Sometimes this skepticism or annoyance took the form of direct action.

Long before the promotion of an official position on sacred imagery under Leo III, images had been on occasion a point of contention. Thus in 588, for example, in an incident reflecting the frustration of the soldiers on the eastern frontier with the imperial authorities’ attempts to reduce their pay, the general Priscus displayed the sacred
mandylion
(towel) from Edessa bearing the image of Christ (called by the Romans
acheiropoiēton,

“not made by human hand”) in an attempt to quell the rioting troops. But the soldiers are reported by the near-contemporary historian Theophylact Simocatta to have hurled stones at the image, seeing through the attempt to overawe them, before later attacking the images of the emperor Maurice himself.
Neither did the angry soldiers show any respect to the bishops of Constantina and Edessa who were sent to calm them.

Over a century later, during the siege of Nicaea by the Arabs in 727, a soldier hurled a stone at an image of the Virgin and damaged it. The motives for his attack are ascribed by the chronicler Theophanes (who reported the incident in his
Chronographia

just under a century afterward) to the soldier’s impiety and iconoclastic sentiment; yet, assuming the event happened at all, it is far more likely that it was a symptom of frustration— whether at the naivety of the population or of soldiers who believed the image would help them or a reflection of the soldier’s own anger will never be known.
这类事件是否比史料记载的更常见，无论如何，它们都表明，虔敬和对教会、宗教象征以及权威的敬重历来取决于处境。即使在同一个信仰体系内部，人们对信仰的持守，以及不同个人或群体践行信念的方式，也可能很不相同。我们不能急于假定人们一概被动地接受了既有的结构或政治与意识形态秩序。
以基督教罗马帝国为代表的统摄一切的信仰体系，是一股强大的统一力量。官方的政治和神学论说，以及一系列较不正式的表达，都体现了这股力量。然而，在人们信仰和行动的方式之内及相互之间，仍有空间容得下其他思路。比如，人们在教堂的举止并不完全符合我们想象中教士所期望的虔敬。诸如此类的事并未挑战基督教信仰与帝国国家本身，却使种种并不总与官方所认可的观点完全一致的理解和信念能够并存。

Whether or not such incidents took place more frequently than the sources record, they demonstrate that piety and respect for the church, for religious symbols, and for authority always depended upon context, and that observance of a faith and how individuals or groups practiced their beliefs could vary, often considerably, within a single system. We should not be overly hasty in assuming a uniform and passive acceptance of the established structures or political-ideological order.

While the overarching belief system represented by the Christian Roman Empire served as a powerful unifying force, reflected in both official political and theological as well as a whole range of less formal forms of discourse, there was space for other ways of thinking within and between these modes of believing and doing— for modes of behavior in church, for example, not entirely consistent with the forms of piety we may imagine to have been desired by the clergy. These were challenges not to the edifice of Christian belief and the imperial state as such, but they nevertheless permitted the coexistence of perceptions and beliefs that were not always entirely consonant with officially sanctioned views.
遵奉、“正统”与异端
Conformity, “Orthodoxy,” and Heterodoxy

到了七世纪后半叶，在这些核心领土上，拜占庭社会与正统基督教文化究竟有多一致，又有多“正统”？一种特定的“东罗马”认同确实存在，凭借这种认同，可以把中世纪早期东罗马帝国的人口描述为一个“正统”的罗马共同体。但“认同”首先是一套有实际功能、通过行为表现出来的策略，情形与语境决定了人们会唤起哪些要素，又会如何组合它们。认同有许多子类，有的反映地方上的文化、语言或族群传统与生活方式，有的反映异端信仰，有的反映社会地位与处境，有的则混合了所有这些要素。任何认同的要义，在于把以特定方式描述自己的人，同不如此自称或可被描述为“他者”、在某些根本方面有别的人区分开来。有些认同涵盖整个文化体系，成为其他更具地方性与个人色彩的认同得以起作用的背景与环境，而后者主宰着大多数人的日常生活和活动。

因此，“基督徒／罗马人”的观念虽在某种程度上是一种力求普遍适用的论说，它对不同社会文化群体所起的作用却不一样，也只有在非常特定的处境、特定的时刻才凸显出来或被人援引。一方面，它首先代表社会精英的自我认同与既有利益，他们继续效忠于现状，对于国家和整个帝国体制的存续至关重要。另一方面，它标出了所有自认属于基督徒罗马世界的人，与外部人群（异教徒、蛮族等等）的区别。以那些被认为身在这个世界之外的人为对照，这种认同也可以代表罗马皇帝的所有臣民和罗马帝国的所有居民，无论出身低微还是精英。换言之，这一特定观念的要素显然深入社会基层，无论在首都周边地区还是在更远的行省，即便仅仅表现为铸有皇帝像的钱币。
然而，运用罗马人认同这一概念须谨慎，因为在不同的社会与文化处境下、面对不同的眼前需求，它具有不同的作用。
遗憾的是，在不得不直面入侵者的关键时刻，普通共同体与行省里的普通人，包括农夫、农民、牧人、手艺人和工匠，是否曾诉诸这种认同，我们难以有把握地断言。他们大概是这么做了，因为这种认同把敌人与遭受袭击者区分开来。包括七世纪圣德米特里乌斯和圣狄奥多尔的奇迹集在内，一些圣徒传记颇为明白地体现了这一点。

How uniform, how “orthodox,” was Byzantine society and Christian orthodox culture in these core territories by the later seventh century? A specifically “east Roman” identity certainly existed, within which the population of the early medieval eastern Roman empire could be represented as an “orthodox” and Roman community. But “identity” is above all functional and performative, a set of operational strategies in which situation and context determine which elements are invoked in which combinations: many subsets of identity exist, some reflecting regional cultural, linguistic, or ethnic traditions and lifeways; some heterodox beliefs; some social status and situations; some a mix of all of these. The crucial point about any identity is that it differentiates those who self-describe in a particular way from those who do not so describe or who can be described as “other,” as different in some fundamental way. Some identities embrace a whole cultural system and serve as a backdrop against and within which other more localized and personalized identities operate, identities that dominate the day- to-day lives and activities of most people.

Thus, while the notion of “Christian/Roman” itself was to a degree a universalizing discourse, it served different sociocultural groups in different ways and came to prominence or was invoked only under certain very specific circumstances and at particular moments. On the one hand, it represented above all the self-identity and vested interests of the social elite whose continued loyalty to the status quo was essential to the survival of the state and the whole imperial edifice. On the other, it represented the difference between all those who understood themselves as members of the Christian Roman world and those outside it— pagans, barbarians, whatever. And it could also represent the identity of all subjects of the Roman emperor and all inhabitants of the Roman Empire, humble or elite, when contrasted with those perceived to stand outside of the boundaries of this world. In other words, while elements of this particular notion clearly penetrated to the roots of society, both in the metropolitan regions as well as in the more distant provinces (even if only in the form of coins bearing the emperor’s image),
the notion of a Roman identity needs to be deployed with care, since it had different valences according to social and cultural circumstances and according to the demands of the moment.

And unfortunately, we cannot really say with any confidence whether or not it was invoked in ordinary communities and among ordinary people— farmers, peasants, herdsmen, artisans, and craftsmen in the provinces—at those crucial moments when they had to face the invader. It probably was, since it demarcated the enemy from those they attacked, and this is fairly clearly expressed in some of the hagiographical literature, including the seventh-century miracle collections of St. Demetrius and those of St. Theodore.

教会是晚期罗马和拜占庭世界在意识形态和经济上最有力量的机构之一。它通过教士和教会等级体系所体现的正式教导与礼仪历，在社会各个层面代表唯一正确的信仰形式。然而，我们已经看到，东罗马基督教的信仰结构内部存在显著差异，例如圣徒崇拜，以及对帝国权威和宗教权威象征的态度。五六会议教规揭示了帝国教会及其官方意识形态表象之下的参差。教会根据正式法令和会议决议推动施行的“正统”的正式定义，以及正式“正确”的正统行为规范，都不断受到挑战。

The Church represented one of the most powerful ideological and economic institutions of the late Roman and Byzantine world. It represented at every level of society the single correct form of belief, through its formal teaching and liturgical calendar, embodied in the clergy and the ecclesiastical hierarchy. But we have already seen that there existed significant variations within the fabric of eastern Roman Christian belief: in respect of the cult of saints, for example, as well as in respect of attitudes to symbols of imperial and religious authority. The lack of uniformity behind the veil of the imperial church and its official ideology is revealed in the canons of the Quinisext council, which make clear that there were ongoing challenges to the formal definitions of “orthodoxy” and to the formally “correct” modes of orthodox behavior that the church promoted through official acts and conciliar decisions.
整个拜占庭时期，知名教士和神学家所编的形形色色的异端信仰名录屡次重编、扩充。这证明抵制各种背离正统的信仰与异端教义极其重要，同样重要的是，明确并细化应当怎样理解、实施和传授“正统”及其相应的实践。
耶路撒冷的索弗罗尼乌斯牧首在630年代、忏悔者马克西姆在630至640年代，以及西奈的阿纳斯塔修斯和八世纪上半叶的大马士革的约翰，都撰写过论辨异端的著作。这类著作自然都以对什么构成正统的预设为基础。
君士坦丁堡的格尔马努斯名下也有一篇辨异端论著，但已证实出自他人之手，主体很可能早在692年五六会议之前就已写成。
一方面，教会会议的记录与精深的神学论著界定了关键教义。另一方面，种类繁多的讲道和礼仪文献与这些会议文献一起，向信徒阐明、解释怎样将神学化为日常的实践和对周围世界的理解。教会还非常详细地规定了信仰偏离正统的人应该如何重返教会，或首次加入教会。经由洗礼而被社会接纳，是归属于基督徒共同体以及罗马共同体的重要一环。

然而在实际生活中，在神学论说所展现的统一体系之下，拜占庭基督教的日常实践包含了多种解释基本教义的方式。基督教在不同文化传统中发展，并施加于这些传统之上，而从这些传统继承来的信仰模式又影响了基督教实践。这种多样性如何体现为社会分化，只能从非常笼统的层面描述。例如，社会经济地位和文化地位不同的人，会在投入财富、时间和精力的程度与选择上显出差异，包括捐助教堂的装饰或营建，参加围绕某个圣徒或殉道者组织的宗教团体，等等。

The frequent repetitions and elaborations on lists of various heretical beliefs that were produced by leading churchmen and theologians throughout the Byzantine period testify to the crucial importance both of combating heterodox and heretical beliefs as well as of defining and refining the way in which “orthodoxy” and its attendant practice were to be understood, applied, and taught.

The patriarch Sophronius of Jerusalem in the 630s, Maximus the Confessor in the 630s–640s, and Anastasius of Sinai as well as John of Damascus in the first half of the eighth century, all produced heresiological works, works that by definition worked with an assumption about what constituted orthodoxy.

Germanus of Constantinople is likewise attributed with a heresiological tract (although this has been shown to be by another hand and the main body of the tract was probably compiled before the Quinisext council of 692).

The acts of church councils, on the one hand, and sophisticated theological texts, on the other, served to define key tenets; and alongside the conciliar texts a wide range of homiletic and liturgical literature helped clarify and explain for believers how theology was to be translated into the daily practice and understanding of the world around them. The church specified in great detail how heterodox believers were to be readmitted or admitted for the first time to the church— social inclusion through baptism was an important element of belonging both to the Christian as well as to the Roman community.

But in practical terms, the day- to-day practice of Byzantine Christianity incorporated, under the unifying system presented in theological discourse, a plurality of ways of interpreting basic tenets, influenced by the inherited patterns of belief from the various cultural traditions in which it developed and upon which it had been imposed. How this plurality was reflected in terms of social differentiation can only be described in very broad terms, through the differences in the degree and choice of investment of wealth, time, and energy made by individuals of different socioeconomic and cultural status, for example—in the endowment of church decoration or building, in membership of a religious organization focused on a saint or martyr, and so forth.

因此，东罗马世界在地域与文化上的多样性，意味着在许多地区，传统的、基督教以前的或非基督教的实践可以无人察觉地延续数百年，虽只存在于孤立、范围相对有限的群体中。异端教义与背离正统的观点，是教会与皇帝不得不一直应对的问题。教会试图处理许多它不认同的信仰与实践，有些看似微不足道，例如五六会议第96条教规禁止男人“把头发梳成繁复的发辫，以引诱心志不稳的人”。同样，背离正统的信仰也可能演变成对皇权的重大挑战，有时的确如此。异端一旦公开显露，就会被视同政治叛逆。这样一来，宗教与灵性领域同世俗意识形态领域混在一起，帝国政府直接卷入了由此引发的问题。地方教会会议与普世教会会议试图处理异端的一些成因，例如偏远地区的教士缺乏纪律或监督，某些基层教士和普通民众无知，或有移民群体到来，对基督教基本要义有不同的观点或理解。教会在这方面一直有所行动，往往并不张扬。
五六会议就如何接纳异端入教立了规定。七世纪后半叶人口大幅流动与变动，使这个问题变得尖锐。第95条教规指出：“至于以浸水方式施洗的欧诺米乌派、在这里称为弗里吉亚派的孟他努派、撒伯流派……以及其他所有异端，本地颇多，尤以来自加拉太境内者为多……”

The geographical and cultural variety of the east Roman world thus meant that in many regions traditional, pre- or non-Christian practices could linger on unobserved for centuries, albeit in isolated and relatively limited groups. Heresy and heterodoxy were two of the constant issues that the Church, and the emperors, had to confront. The church tried to deal with a whole range of beliefs and practices with which it did not approve, some seemingly trivial— canon 96 of the Quinisext forbids men to “arrange their hair in elaborate plaits, offering allurements to unstable minds,” for example. By the same token, heterodox beliefs could evolve that might, and did in some cases, develop into major challenges to the imperial authority. Heresy, at least when it made its presence obvious, was equated with political treason, conflating the religious-spiritual with the secular ideological spheres, and directly involving the imperial government in the issues thus raised. Local synods and ecumenical councils tried to grapple with some of the causes of heresy, such as the lack of clerical discipline or supervision in far-flung regions, the ignorance of some of the lower clergy as well as of the ordinary populace, or the arrival of immigrant population groups with different views or different understanding of the basic elements of Christianity. The church was constantly active in this respect, often on a very low-key basis.

The Quinisext legislates on the admission of heretics to the church, an issue that had become acute as a result of considerable demographic disturbances in the later seventh century. Canon 95 notes: “In the case of Eunomians, however, who are baptized by immersion, and Montanists, referred to here as Phrygians, and Sabellians. . . as well as all the other heretics— there are many here, especially those from the land of Galatia—.”

七世纪东部行省落入阿拉伯人手中，为当时的皇帝所面临的一个最棘手的神学与政治问题提供了部分的实际解决办法，即如何消除卡尔西顿派（二性论派）基督徒同叙利亚、埃及的一性论派之间日积月累的敌视和猜疑。然而，君士坦丁堡没有放弃有朝一日收复失地的想法，问题也就并未消失。更重要的是，君士坦丁堡牧首座仍须与东方的姊妹教会，以及其自身所辖、如今却处在帝国控制范围之外的教省打交道。一志论最终未能成功，民众却颇有支持与认同。帝国政策发生了根本转向，这一转变受到严厉、甚至有几分残酷的强制推行，才是一志论失败的原因。整个经过清楚说明，国家在教义问题上居于中心地位，并为推行一种官方立场而卷入纷争。然而680—681年会议之后，基督论争议便不再扰动帝国教会。唯有八、九世纪的反圣像政策（后来也涉及基督论）才引起新的内部重大分裂。至少在九、十世纪拥护圣像者改写这段历史之前，双方各自是否有超过寥寥数人的关注或投入，仍很难判断。

The loss of the eastern provinces to the Arabs in the seventh century offered a partial practical solution to one of the most difficult theological-political issues faced by the emperors of the period: how to overcome the hostility and suspicion that had evolved between the Chalcedonian, or dyophisite, Christians and the miaphysites of Syria and Egypt. But since Constantinople did not give up on the idea that the lost territories would at some point be recovered, the problem did not go away. More importantly, the Constantinopolitan patriarchate still had to deal with its sister churches in the east as well as ecclesiastical provinces under its own authority, which now lay outside of imperial control. While monotheletism ultimately failed, this was not because it had no support or purchase among the population—quite the contrary. Rather, there took place a radical shift in imperial policy, a shift that was rigorously and to a degree brutally enforced. The whole story offers a good example of how the state was central to matters of dogma, and how it was embroiled in the imposition of an official position. But after the council of 680–681, Christological issues no longer rocked the imperial church. Only the iconoclastic policies of the eighth and ninth centuries— which also had, eventually, a Christological element— stimulated further major internal rifts, and it is by no means clear that these commanded the interest or commitment of more than a handful on either side, at least until the iconophiles rewrote the history of the period during the ninth and tenth centuries.

七世纪下半叶和八世纪初的一些著作，让我们得以窥见教会所面对的地方差异有多大，以及各地对基督教基本教导的接受程度有何不同。我们已见过一些信仰或行为有别于正统的例子。归于云游修士西奈的阿纳斯塔修斯名下的那部引人入胜的“问答录”，提供了关于当时普通基督徒忧虑与关切的珍贵资料。阿纳斯塔修斯似乎从未到访小亚细亚的行省，但人们向他提出的各类问题，可视为反映了包括安纳托利亚在内的各东部行省居民的许多关切。他们关心何种行为合乎洁净规条，在非基督徒统治者治下怎样敬拜，多长时间该领一次圣餐。他们也关心更广泛的世局，例如阿拉伯人为何获胜、基督徒缘何战败，或穷人的子女何以多而富人子女少，饮食与健康、正确信仰与胜利、犯罪与上帝的惩罚之间又有何联系。实际上，罪与罚的母题在普通信徒中极为常见。通俗的圣徒传、布道辞，以及我们已见过的启示文学和神学家等人提出的解释，都有这一主题。

An insight into the degree of local variation and the different levels of engagement with basic Christian teaching that the church had to contend with is afforded by some writings of the second half of the seventh and early eighth centuries. We have already seen some examples of dissident belief or behavior. The fascinating collection of “questions and answers” attributed to the wandering monk Anastasius of Sinai provides invaluable information about the worries and concerns of ordinary Christians at this time. Anastasius seems never to have visited the provinces of Asia Minor, but the sorts of issues put to him can be taken to reflect many of the concerns of people across the eastern provinces, including Anatolia. People were concerned about rules of purity, about how to worship under a non-Christian ruler, about how often they should take communion, about the state of the world more broadly, about the reasons for Arab victory and Christian defeat, about such things as why the poor have many children and the wealthy few, about the connections between diet and health, or between correct belief and success or sinful behavior and divine punishment. Indeed, the motif of sin and punishment was an extremely common theme among ordinary believers, appearing in popular hagiographical writing, in sermons, and, as we have seen, in apocalyptic writing as well as in the explanations offered by theologians and others.
考虑到时局对东罗马政府的政治权力构成的限制，政府在监管或处置异议、控制异议来源方面，看来取得了相当显著的成效。这一点不应忽略。例如，680—681年君士坦丁堡会议之后，支持一志论的文学与著述似乎几乎全被销毁或压了下来，连662年在君士坦丁堡召开的那场重要的教会会议的记录也不例外。
我们仅能凭帝国境内外文献中偶尔间接的提及，得知这些材料曾存在，其中包括一些保存在叙利亚西北信奉一志论地区的叙利亚文版本。680—681年会议接近尾声时，一些部队和他们的领袖以行动表示反对；其中尤以安纳托利孔军统帅利奥为代表。这样的反对尚未成势，就遭到了无情的镇压，军队被遣回各自行省的驻地。
而在这场会议以前，帝国官方政策还奉行一志论时，当局曾搜查、销毁忏悔者马克西姆等政策反对者的著述，并把传播或收藏它们的人列为怀疑对象。
第一和第二次反圣像运动（730—787年及815—841年）之后，类似的情形又出现了。当时帝国教会和政府看来相当成功地查出并销毁了反圣像的文献。反圣像皇帝在815年至830年代的政府似乎也同样成功地查出并控制了异议者，这一时期的证据比第一次反圣像运动期间略为充分。
同样，帝国官员经常能截住人员及文书，例如在640年代、650年代或720年代，教皇的使者和携带信件的私人会被拦下、搜查，有时还会被逮捕。例如，反对帝国一志论的狄奥多尔与欧普雷皮乌斯两兄弟，648年试图出发前往罗马时在阿拜多斯被捕。
为避免这类问题，640年代反对帝国一志论的重要人物多尔的斯特凡诺斯，不得不取道北非，从罗马去巴勒斯坦。他说：“他们向各地、各行省发出关乎我的命令，要求逮捕我，给我戴上锁链，送交他们。”

We should not lose sight of the fact that the east Roman government seems to have been remarkably successful, given the constraints on its political authority imposed by circumstances, in policing or managing dissent and in controlling the sources of dissent. After the council of 680–681 in Constantinople, for example, it seems that nearly all traces of promonothelete literature and writing was destroyed or suppressed, including the records from an important synod of the church held in Constantinople in 662.

We know of their existence only through occasional oblique references in texts from both within as well as outside the empire, including the Syriac versions of some of this material that survived in the monothelete regions of northwest Syria. What potential opposition there was toward the end of the council— voiced in the activities of some military units and their leaders, in particular the commander of the Anatolikon forces, Leo— was ruthlessly crushed and the troops sent back to their provincial bases.

And before the council of 680–681, when official imperial policy was itself monothelete, the writings of Maximus the Confessor himself, among other opponents of imperial policy, were sought out and destroyed, just as those who circulated or kept them were suspects in the eyes of the imperial authorities.

A similar situation prevailed after the first and second periods of iconoclasm (730–787 and 815–841), when it seems that the imperial church and the government were very successful in hunting out iconoclastic material and destroying it, just as the governments of the iconoclast emperors in the period 815–830s, when we have somewhat better evidence than from the first period of iconoclasm, appear to have been equally successful in locating and controlling dissidents.

By the same token, imperial officials were frequently able to intercept both people and documents, for example, in the 640s and 650s or in the 720s, when papal emissaries as well as private persons carrying letters were held up, searched, and on occasion arrested. The brothers Theodore and Euprepius, opponents of imperial monotheletism, were arrested at Abydos in 648, trying to leave for Rome, for example.

To avoid such problems in the 640s, Stephen of Dor, a key figure in the opposition to imperial monotheletism, had to travel from Rome to Palestine via North Africa, for example: “They sent out orders concerning me by place and province, that I should be arrested and delivered up to them in chains.”
人们或许会想，现代国家拥有工业监视技术的种种便利，前现代国家要同样严密、有效地控制边界，总是很难的。然而，大多数需要长途旅行的人，即便不为有伴，也单为安全而愿意结伴行走，这让边境管理容易得多。这些旅行团体需要雇向导，或为自己、行李和随行仆役雇用各种交通工具，因而相对容易管理和监视。

It might be thought that it would be difficult for a premodern state to control its borders as carefully and as efficiently as a modern state, with all the advantages of industrial surveillance technology at its disposal. But it was made much easier by virtue of the fact that most people who wished to travel across substantial distances preferred to do so in a group simply for reasons of safety, if not for companionship. Such groups of travelers were dependent on hiring guides or various modes of transport for themselves and their baggage and accompanying servants and were relatively easy to manage and to monitor.

当然，个人能悄悄越过边境或避开出入关卡，无疑也确有人这么做。但这么做总是极其危险，可能招来灾祸，如遭抢劫、被掳为奴或被捕，最坏还会丧命。至690年代为止，必定有若干地区可以这样越境，尤其安纳托利亚和巴尔干的“前沿”或边境地区，无疑很容易相互通行。在黎凡特沿海，拜占庭海军的活动和袭扰在640年代、650年代初以及670年代后期都是重要因素。当时一些地方和城镇或许处于某种政治真空，谁的军队眼下在那里就承认谁的权威，对个人往来则几乎不加管束。钱币证据也许支持这一点。帝国铸造的铜币继续在叙利亚北部流通，数量之多，无疑会便利帝国辖地与原属帝国的地区继续往来。

Of course individuals could, and no doubt did, manage to slip across frontiers or avoid points of egress and access, but this was always extremely risky and could end in disaster— robbery, enslavement, or capture—at worst, death. There were certainly in the period up to the 690s, a number of regions where this would have been possible, especially as the Anatolian and Balkan “frontier” or border regions were undoubtedly highly permeable, while along the Levantine coast, where Byzantine naval activity and raiding was a significant factor in the 640s and early 650s and again in the later 670s, a number of districts and towns probably existed in a partial political vacuum, acknowledging whichever military power was currently present and permitting the movement of individuals with very little control. The numismatic evidence may support this, given the continuing presence of imperially minted copper coinage in northern Syria in quantities that would undoubtedly have facilitated ongoing relations between imperial and former imperial districts.
不过，在有必要时，旅行团体更容易监视，混在其中、想躲开帝国官员耳目的人也更易发现。晚期罗马政府有效控制了进出帝国的主要关口，
当时形成的安排，似乎一直沿用至拜占庭时期后段而没有中断。一般说来，每个旅行者都需要准许离境的正式文书。教士即使在帝国境内旅行，也需要上司出具正式信函（
grammata
）。此类文书以拉丁语称为
formatae
或
epistulae formatae
，例如从一个教省赴另一个教省，或造访都城时都不可缺少。教会法为此一再强调，虽然有限的证据表明，这类规条时常被忽略或滥用。
对平信徒而言，这类文书被称作
sigillia
或
sigillia kai sphragides
，即“加盖印信或经验证的文书”。一些事例表明，没有这些文书，旅行者可能遭遇严重麻烦。七世纪亚美尼亚编年史家塞贝奥斯认为，帝国当局为逮捕出逃的高级将领而监视道路和堡垒，并非不可信。
例如九世纪初，德卡波利斯的圣格里高利未带文书到达一个港口，就因涉嫌替阿拉伯人刺探情报而被捕。
境内行旅，特别是使用
dromos
或
cursus publicus
（公共驿传）时，须由当局签发相应的文书和许可（不过法令同样清楚表明，此事极易被滥用）。
行省教士与国家官员，尤其是税务官员，合作紧密，甚至使政府能够立法强迫寡妇与外国俘虏（大概年龄须相当）结婚，以使税款能够继续缴纳。
帝国官员搜集情报与监视个人同样有效率。他们管控传入阿拉伯领土的情报，可能使人遭到为敌方刺探情报或煽动反对帝国政府的指控。650年代忏悔者马克西姆的事就是如此，尽管地理背景很不一样。

Nevertheless, groups of travelers were more readily monitored, when necessary, and individuals who wished to escape the notice of the imperial officials traveling in such parties were easier to detect. The late Roman government controlled key points of entry or exit from the empire efficiently,

and the arrangements that had evolved appear to have been maintained without a break well into the later Byzantine period. Each traveler generally required formal letters authorizing their departure. For churchmen even within the empire, official letters
(grammata)
from their superiors were required. Such documents— referred to as
formatae
or
epistulae formatae

in Latin— were necessary when moving from one episcopal province to another, for example, or when visiting the capital, as canon law stresses repeatedly— although the limited evidence indicates that such regulations were frequently ignored or abused.
For laypersons, these papers were known as
sigillia

The close cooperation between provincial clergy and state officials, particularly fiscal officials, even made it possible for the government to legislate to compel widows to marry foreign captives (presumably of an appropriate age) in order to support continued payment of taxes.

Imperial officials were efficient in gathering information as well as in keeping watch on individuals, and control over information that was taken into Arab territory could lead to accusations of spying or instigating opposition to the imperial government—as we have already seen, this was the case, albeit in a very different geographical context, with Maximus the Confessor in the 650s.
要辨明帝国各行省信仰和实践的统一程度，或它们对规范的遵从程度，还要考虑另一个使问题复杂化的因素。自七世纪中叶至九世纪，帝国政府实行迁移人口的政策，有时人数极多，把居民从小亚细亚一些地区迁往巴尔干，或反向迁移，以重新充实遭到破坏地区的人口。这项政策无疑有经济上的好处，却也成为背离正统的观点从帝国一地传入另一地的有效渠道，因而教会管辖地方人口时必须始终保持警惕。

除了较重要的异端运动，教会还须应对许多影响较小的非正统信仰。除五六会议教规所反映的实际情形外，我们几乎无从得知教会怎样应对。例如，吕考尼亚和弗里吉亚的阿廷加尼人可能甚至并非基督徒，但到九世纪初似乎仍很兴盛。又如东安纳托利亚的保罗派，据载自七世纪起，经过整个八世纪直至九世纪，都受到教会与国家的干预，却似乎一直存续下来。七世纪及其后的几个世纪里，当局曾试图让他们改宗或重新受洗，也曾迫害并试图消灭他们的领袖。这表明安纳托利亚存在各种信条，其中有些未必能与二性论基督教的基本教义相容，保罗派就是一例。
帝国与哈里发国及其相抗衡的宗教几乎一直处于冲突中，在这样的情形下，人们显然看到了非正统信仰的危险。然而人们归于这些危险的种种后果是否真实存在，仍是一个待议的问题。

There is a further complicating factor in respect of distinguishing levels of uniformity or conformity of belief and practice across the provinces of the empire. In the period from the middle of the seventh through into the ninth century the imperial government followed a policy of moving populations— sometimes in huge numbers— from parts of Asia Minor to the Balkans and vice versa in order to repopulate devastated regions. While it no doubt had economic benefits, it also proved an effective means by which heterodox views were transferred from one region of the empire to another, so the church had to be constantly vigilant in its managing of local populations.

And quite apart from the more important heretical movements, the church had to combat many less significant heterodox beliefs. We know next to nothing about how it tackled such issues, apart from the reflection of reality in the canons of the Quinisext. But the fact that groups such as the Athingani (in Lycaonia and Phrygia), who may not even have been Christian, were still apparently flourishing in the early ninth century, or that the Paulicians in eastern Anatolia appear to have continued to exist in spite of reported interventions from both church and state from the seventh and throughout the eighth into the ninth century (there were attempts to convert or rebaptize them as well as to persecute and destroy their leadership in the seventh century and in the following centuries) shows that Anatolia contained a variety of creeds not necessarily (as with the Paulicians) reconcilable with the basic tenets of dyophysite Christianity.

The dangers of heterodoxy in the context of near-constant conflict with the caliphate and a rival religion were clearly recognized, although whether these dangers carried with them all the implications that have been ascribed to them is yet another question that remains at issue.
最后，教会也必须面对犹太教。基督教自诞生之初就与犹太教有着复杂的关系。按基督徒的看法，犹太人因不承认弥赛亚而丧失了选民的地位，而这一地位如今已转给了罗马人，双方关系因此格外复杂。自七世纪中叶起，反犹论辩尤其突出。基督徒似乎写下一批文献，为敬奉十字架、圣髑、崇拜圣徒等关键实践辩护，以回应基督徒崇拜偶像的指控。
有人认为，其中一些论辩也回应了伊斯兰教在早期对基督教信仰与实践的批评。这一点仍有争论，不过基督教的论辩在整个七世纪显然变得格外激烈，反映了被征服行省和帝国境内的基督徒日益艰难的处境。
还有人提出，阿廷加尼人代表了一个犹太化的教派。

总的来说，直到六世纪，官方仍容许犹太人存在，尽管他们往往受到严重的歧视。然而，自查士丁尼在位以来，他们在罗马世界越来越孤立。波斯人继而阿拉伯人的征服，令这一过程大大加剧，因为有些人认为犹太人对这些征服负有部分责任。东罗马文化似乎在以封闭和防御的姿态回应七世纪灾难性的领土损失与战败，而这一发展正是这种姿态的体现。希拉克略在位时，后来很可能也在利奥三世在位时，当局曾对犹太人施行强制洗礼。犹太人不得参加许多公共活动，不得以任何形式参与国家事务，帝国无论遭逢什么灾祸，也常常把责任归到他们身上。遭到这种待遇的还有别的群体，常有各种异端群体与他们并列，但犹太人一再被单独挑出来加以苛待。

Finally, the church also had to contend with Judaism, a religion with which Christianity had from its very beginnings an ambiguous relationship, the more so since the Jews, by failing to acknowledge the Messiah, had lost their status as the Chosen People, which had now been transferred to the Romans. Anti-Jewish polemic becomes especially prominent from the middle of the seventh century; indeed, Christian texts defending a range of key practices— devotion to the Cross, to relics, the cult of saints, for example— appear to have been composed to answer accusations that Christians were idolaters.

Some of this has been assumed to respond also to early Islamic criticism of Christian belief and practice, and although this remains debated, it seems clear that the Christian polemic becomes especially strident in the course of the seventh century, reflecting the increasingly difficult circumstances in which Christians in the conquered provinces as well as in the empire found themselves.
It has also been suggested that the Athingani represent a Judaizing sect.

In general, until the sixth century, Jews were officially tolerated, although often treated with considerable prejudice. From the reign of Justinian, however, they became increasingly isolated within the Roman world, a process greatly exacerbated by the results of the Persian and then the Arab conquests, for which the Jews were partially held to be responsible, and a development that reflects the introversion and defensiveness with which east Roman culture seems to have responded to the catastrophic losses and defeats of the seventh century. Compulsory baptisms of Jews were carried out under Heraclius and later (probably) under Leo III. Jews were prohibited from a wide range of public activities as well as participation in the state in any form and were frequently blamed for whatever ills befell the empire. While they were not alone in this, since various heretical groups were usually listed alongside them, they were regularly singled out for ill-treatment.

五六会议共定下102条教规，其中屡次涉及背离正统的信仰和实践。这足以说明，即使大多数共同体自认或自称“正统”，安纳托利亚各地的基督教礼仪实践与敬拜方式依然有很大差异。这些差异让教会和国家都感到忧虑。这里重要的是，这些群体，无论犹太人、孟他努派还是其他群体，因为不接受占主导地位的宗教意识形态，其“罗马人”身份遭到了怀疑。犹太人一再被单独挑出来，这一点倒在其次。查士丁尼在位时，他们在基督教罗马的理论中仍有特定的位置，是基督徒对《旧约》与《新约》所作解释的活证据。自其继承者起，这一地位很快削弱。由于他们被视为心怀敌意、暗中反对，就连他们是否属于东罗马帝国也成了问题，他们成了潜在敌人，一支潜伏在帝国内部的第五纵队。就此而言，帝国政府和教会依然有能力监管人们的信仰和可读的书籍，想必显得格外重要，不管这种监督实际上有多少漏洞。下一章将讨论，世俗法律和教会法如何影响人们对世界的看法，以及政治和文化边界的重划给他们造成了什么影响。

The number of repetitions dealing with heterodox belief and practice that occur among the 102 canons of the Quinisext is a sufficient demonstration of the fact that, even if most communities identified with or claimed to be “orthodox” in their own view, there remained substantial variations in Christian liturgical practice and worship across Anatolia, and that such differences were looked upon with some concern by both church and state. But what is important is not the fact that Jews, rather than any other identifiable group, continued to be singled out: rather, by failing to accept the dominant religious ideological system, the “Roman” identity of such groups— Jews, Montanists, or others— was placed in doubt. Whereas under Justinian they had still held a particular place in Christian Roman theory—as a living proof of the Christian interpretation of the Old and New Testaments— this position was rapidly eroded from the time of his successors onward. Their implicit or tacit hostility and opposition jeopardized their belonging to the East Roman Empire at all and made them potential enemies, a fifth column within the empire. The continuing ability of the imperial government and the church to police people’s beliefs and what they could read, however imperfect this oversight actually was, must have seemed particularly important in this respect. In the following chapter we will look at the ways in which secular and canon law affected how people saw their world, and how the redrawing of political and cultural boundaries affected them.
